To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the IceCube atmospheric muon-track events can be used to bound the LSND and/or MiniBooNE oscillations; (ii) the IceCube sensitivity is enhanced by binning in energy; (iii) the IceCube bound on the LSND/MiniBooNE mixing element can be improved in the future by collecting more data and by using the information on the muon energy

the IceCube data collected in the past 3-4 years can exclude the LSND and the MiniBooNE results and that the future IceCube data (with 10 years of running) can establish the bound on Uμ4 with the 99% C.L. at the level of 0.005.

the IceCube atmospheric νμ → νs data can be used to restrict the LSND and/or MiniBooNE νs at the 3σ level, and that the bound on |Uμ4||2 is improved by a factor of 3-5 when the zenith angle and energy of events are taken into account.

the sterile neutrinos are not required to explain the LSND and/or MiniBooNE results and the IceCube atmospheric νμ − νs oscillations are not observed at the level of sensitivity of LSND and MiniBOONE.
the IceCube atmospheric data can exclude the sterile neutrino interpretation of LSND and Mini BooNE at the 3-5σ confidence level.
LSND and Mini-BooNE are excluded by the IceCube data at 99% CL, and that the IceCube data are consistent with the standard three neutrino scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IceCube data can be used to exclude the LSND andMiniBooNE sterile-neutrino hypothesis at 4-σ level.
the IceCube atmospheric data can be used to exclude the LSND and/or MiniBooNE mixing at (4–8)σ C.L., depending on the assumed energy binning and the value of Uτ4.
the IceCube atmospheric data can provide an important complementary constraint on the LSND andMiniBooNE sterile-neutrino hypothesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the atmospheric neutrino data can be used to probe the sterile neutrino mixing in the energy region which is inaccessible to the reactor and accelerator experiments.
the atmospheric neutrinos provide an independent and complementary way to test the LSND and/or MiniBooNE results and the IceCube can be used to probe the eV-scale sterile neutrinos in the future.
the IceCube atmospheric data can provide the strongest bound on |Uμ4|(2) among the existing experiments and can be competitive with the future reactor neutrino experiments.
